links.outcome: Re-identification risk and semantic similarity of de-identified psychiatric narratives versus an LLM-only rewriting baseline
links.effect: Anonpsy achieved consistently low re-identification risk under expert, semantic, and GPT-5 evaluations, with substantially lower semantic similarity and identifiability than the LLM-only baseline. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Compared with a strong LLM-only rewriting baseline, Anonpsy yields substantially lower semantic similarity and identifiability.

unlisted_practices: Graph-guided semantic rewriting that converts narratives into semantic graphs, perturbs identifying context, and regenerates text with an LLM, to de-identify psychiatric narratives while preserving clinical structure

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates Anonpsy, a graph-constrained safeguard/de-identification framework applied to LLM generation to reduce re-identification risk while preserving clinical utility in psychiatric narratives.
